# PropagationSolver { #clerq.PropagationSolver }

```python
PropagationSolver(
    system=None,
    t_min=0.0,
    t_max=1.0,
    t_steps=100,
    method='mesolve',
    opts=None,
    savefile=None,
    z_min=0.0,
    z_max=1.0,
    z_steps=10,
    z_steps_inner=2,
    num_density_z_func=None,
    num_density_z_args=None,
    interaction_strengths=None,
    velocity_classes=None,
    *,
    atom=None,
    real_drive=False,
)
```

Solver for the propagation of fields through a medium of systems.

Steps the fields through space with a finite-difference method, solving
the Lindblad master equation for the :class:`~clerq.system.System` at
each step (once per velocity class if the medium is Doppler broadened).

## Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name                  | Type                  | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | Default     |
|-----------------------|-----------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------|
| system                | dict \| None          | Dict (or empty dict for defaults) describing the quantum system; passed to :class:`~clerq.system.System`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | `None`      |
| t_min                 | float                 | Start time of the simulation.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | `0.0`       |
| t_max                 | float                 | End time of the simulation.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | `1.0`       |
| t_steps               | int                   | Number of time steps.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | `100`       |
| method                | str                   | Solver method — ``'mesolve'`` (Lindblad master equation) is the only supported value.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | `'mesolve'` |
| opts                  | dict \| None          | Dict of QuTiP solver options.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | `None`      |
| savefile              | str \| None           | Path prefix for caching solved results (``'.qu'`` extension appended automatically). Pass ``None`` to disable caching.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | `None`      |
| z_min                 | float                 | The front of the medium.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | `0.0`       |
| z_max                 | float                 | The back of the medium.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | `1.0`       |
| z_steps               | int                   | Number of space steps at which the solution is recorded.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | `10`        |
| z_steps_inner         | int \| str            | Number of finite-difference steps made within each space step. Pass ``"auto"`` to start from 2 and let ``solve()`` raise it until the estimated step error is below ``step_error_warn`` (see :meth:`solve`).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | `2`         |
| num_density_z_func    | str \| None           | Name of a function in ``clerq.t_funcs`` giving the number density profile over z. Square by default.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | `None`      |
| num_density_z_args    | dict \| None          | Dict of arguments for ``num_density_z_func``.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | `None`      |
| interaction_strengths | list\[float\] \| None | Interaction strength of each field with the medium, one for each field.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | `None`      |
| velocity_classes      | dict \| None          | Dict defining the velocity classes for Doppler broadening, or ``None`` for no broadening. ``thermal_width`` and the ``thermal_delta_*`` values are cyclic frequencies, in the same units as ``decays`` rates and ``rabi_freq``. Instead of ``thermal_delta_steps`` the classes can be given a maximum spacing ``thermal_delta_spacing``, or ``"auto"`` for the largest spacing with no spurious Doppler echo inside the time window (``thermal_delta_auto_spacing()``). The density of the classes is Gaussian, ``exp(-(delta / thermal_width)**2)`` (``thermal_weights``); each class is weighted by this times the detuning interval it represents (``thermal_widths``). | `None`      |
| atom                  | dict \| None          | Deprecated name for ``system``.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | `None`      |
| real_drive            | bool                  | Deprecated. Drive the Hamiltonian with ``Re(Omega)`` only, the behaviour before the complex-envelope drive. That is exact for resonant problems with real fields and a symmetric, equally weighted velocity-class grid, but wrong for a single detuned field (for example a two-level medium, optical depth 6, half-width detuning 2: transmission 1.1 instead of 0.30). The default drives the coupled pair with ``Omega`` and ``conj(Omega)``.                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | `False`     |

### build_zlist { #clerq.PropagationSolver.build_zlist }

```python
PropagationSolver.build_zlist(z_min, z_max, z_steps, z_steps_inner)
```

Builds the space grid.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name          | Type   | Description                                                                                                | Default    |
|---------------|--------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| z_min         | float  | The front of the medium, in your chosen length unit.                                                       | _required_ |
| z_max         | float  | The back of the medium.                                                                                    | _required_ |
| z_steps       | int    | The number of even-spaced steps on which to solve and record the solution.                                 | _required_ |
| z_steps_inner | int    | Between each z_step, make this many inner steps of the finite-difference solver (for numerical stability). | _required_ |

#### Notes {.doc-section .doc-section-notes}

- If the problem requires a lot of space steps for stability, but
    you don't need to record the solution at such a high-level of
    resolution, increase z_steps_inner.

### coherences { #clerq.PropagationSolver.coherences }

```python
PropagationSolver.coherences(coupled_levels)
```

Gets the sum of coherences (off-diagonals) in a list of coupled
    level pairs.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name           | Type                | Description                      | Default    |
|----------------|---------------------|----------------------------------|------------|
| coupled_levels | list\[list\[int\]\] | a list of pairs of level indexes | _required_ |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type       | Description                                           |
|--------|------------|-------------------------------------------------------|
|        | np.ndarray | np.array, shape (z_steps+1, t_steps+1), dtype=complex |

#### Note {.doc-section .doc-section-note}

Unlike ``System.get_fields_sum_coherence``, which operates on a
single-z time series with per-field weighting factors, this method
sums over the full (z, t) array with unit weights.

### init_Omegas_zt { #clerq.PropagationSolver.init_Omegas_zt }

```python
PropagationSolver.init_Omegas_zt()
```

Inits the Rabi frequency array.

_Omegas_zt is the internal angular-frequency field array;
``rabi_freqs_zt`` is its public cyclic view.

_Omegas_zt shape: (num_fields, z_steps+1, t_steps+1) — field-first.
states_zt shape: (z_steps+1, t_steps+1, num_states, num_states) — z-first.
These are inconsistent; correcting either is a breaking API change,
deferred to a future major version.

```python

```

### load_results { #clerq.PropagationSolver.load_results }

```python
PropagationSolver.load_results()
```

Loads the solution from a QuTiP pickle file.

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type       | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
|--------|------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | ValueError | if the savefile was built from a different problem definition (hash mismatch), or was solved with the old factor**2 source-term weights and a field has factors other than 1, or was solved with velocity-class weights that ignored the class spacing on a non-uniform grid, or was solved with the other drive convention (savefiles without a drive marker used ``Re(Omega)``) for a problem where the two differ (static detunings, level energies or an asymmetric class grid). |

#### Notes {.doc-section .doc-section-notes}

- The path from which the results will be loaded is taken from
    self.savefile.
- Old savefiles without metadata are loaded without integrity
    checking, with a warning, unless a field has factors other
    than 1 (see Raises).

### solve { #clerq.PropagationSolver.solve }

```python
PropagationSolver.solve(
    step='ab',
    rho0=None,
    recalc=True,
    progress=True,
    progress_show_area=False,
    check_counter_prop_depletion=True,
    depletion_warn=0.01,
    depletion_error=0.1,
    check_stability=True,
    blowup_factor=1000.0,
    step_error_warn=0.1,
    max_z_steps_inner=512,
    t_step_error_warn=0.1,
    window_edge_warn=0.2,
    window_edge_frac=0.05,
)
```

Solves the propagation of the fields through the medium.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name                         | Type   | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | Default   |
|------------------------------|--------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------|
| step                         | str    | 'euler (for Euler method) or 'ab' (for Adams-Bashforth)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | `'ab'`    |
| rho0                         | Qobj   | the initial density matrix state                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | `None`    |
| recalc                       | bool   | Recalculate the solution even if a savefile exists?                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | `True`    |
| progress                     | bool   | Show a tqdm progress bar with elapsed time, ETA and current max field amplitude.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | `True`    |
| progress_show_area           | bool   | Extend the progress bar with the pulse area ∫\|Ω\|dt for each field at the current z-step.  Requires progress=True.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | `False`   |
| check_counter_prop_depletion | bool   | Run a post-solve depletion check on any counter-propagating fields. Set False to suppress.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | `True`    |
| depletion_warn               | float  | Depletion fraction that triggers a UserWarning.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | `0.01`    |
| depletion_error              | float  | Depletion fraction that raises CounterPropagatingDepletionError.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | `0.1`     |
| check_stability              | bool   | Stop with :class:`PropagationInstabilityError` as soon as the solution blows up (non-finite field, field larger than ``blowup_factor`` times its initial peak, or a failed master-equation integration), and warn if the z-step looks too coarse. Set False to suppress.                                                                                                                                                                   | `True`    |
| blowup_factor                | float  | Growth of the peak field, relative to its peak at ``z_min``, treated as a blow-up. Raise it for media with genuine gain.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | `1000.0`  |
| step_error_warn              | float  | Estimated accumulated relative error (from the differences of dOmega/dz between z-steps, relative to the peak field) above which a UserWarning is issued suggesting a larger ``z_steps_inner``. The largest value seen is kept in ``self.step_error_estimate``. With ``z_steps_inner="auto"`` this is also the tolerance: the solve is repeated with more inner steps until the estimate is below it, or ``max_z_steps_inner`` is reached. | `0.1`     |
| max_z_steps_inner            | int    | Upper limit for ``z_steps_inner="auto"``.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | `512`     |
| t_step_error_warn            | float  | With ``check_stability``, warn if the time grid is too coarse to represent the fields and coherences: the relative error (to the peak) of interpolating them from every other time sample, ``self.t_step_error_estimate``, exceeds this. The error of the full grid is smaller, by about a factor of 16 once the grid resolves the signal (a cubic spline), and by less on a coarser grid.                                                 | `0.1`     |
| window_edge_warn             | float  | With ``check_stability``, warn if a field is still changing near the edge of the time window (the first or last 5% of it) by more than this fraction of its peak, so that a pulse or its ringing is probably cut off. Kept in ``self.window_edge_estimate``.                                                                                                                                                                               | `0.2`     |
| window_edge_frac             | float  | Fraction of the time window at each end that ``window_edge_warn`` looks at. Reduce it if the window deliberately starts or ends in the middle of a pulse.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | `0.05`    |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name      | Type       | Description                                                                                                                                  |
|-----------|------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Omegas_zt | np.ndarray | The solved field complex Rabi frequency at each point in space z and time t, as an *angular* frequency (``rabi_freqs_zt`` times ``2 * pi``). |
|           | np.ndarray | self.states_zt: The solved density matrix at each point in space z and time t.                                                               |

### suggest_t_steps { #clerq.PropagationSolver.suggest_t_steps }

```python
PropagationSolver.suggest_t_steps(
    points_per_period=10.0,
    bandwidth_fraction=0.99,
)
```

Estimate the ``t_steps`` needed to resolve the problem's frequencies.

Finds the largest frequency scale (cyclic, in the units of the problem)
and returns enough steps over ``[t_min, t_max]`` for
``points_per_period`` samples per period of it. The scales are the
bandwidth of the input fields (``bandwidth_fraction`` of their power), their peak Rabi
frequencies combined with the detunings and the Doppler width.

This is an estimate from the input fields: the medium can add structure
(sidebands, ringing), so check the solved result too; ``solve()`` warns
if the grid turns out to be too coarse.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name               | Type   | Description                                                                                                                                                         | Default   |
|--------------------|--------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------|
| points_per_period  | float  | Time samples per period of the fastest scale.                                                                                                                       | `10.0`    |
| bandwidth_fraction | float  | Fraction of an input field's spectral power that its bandwidth must contain. Lower it for sharp-edged pulses, whose slowly decaying tails would otherwise dominate. | `0.99`    |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type   | Description                                                      |
|--------|--------|------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | int    | The suggested number of time steps; compare it with ``t_steps``. |

### thermal_delta_auto_spacing { #clerq.PropagationSolver.thermal_delta_auto_spacing }

```python
PropagationSolver.thermal_delta_auto_spacing()
```

Largest cyclic class spacing free of Doppler echoes in the time window.

Sampling the detuning at spacing ``h`` makes the summed response repeat
at ``t = 1 / h``. That echo is spurious, so it must fall outside the
window of length ``t_max - t_min``; the spacing is
``THERMAL_ECHO_MARGIN`` of the window's reciprocal.

A coherence between two levels oscillates at ``s * Delta`` cyclic, where
``s`` is the sum of the ``factor_doppler_shift`` of the fields that
shift the two levels apart: 1 for a single co-propagating field, 2 for
the two-photon coherence of a co-propagating ladder. Its echo is at
``1 / (s h)``, so the spacing is divided by the largest possible ``s``,
the sum of ``abs(factor_doppler_shift)`` over all the fields.

Decay damps the echo, but this ignores that, so it is safe for any
system.

### to_autodiff { #clerq.PropagationSolver.to_autodiff }

```python
PropagationSolver.to_autodiff(**options)
```

Return a differentiable version of this problem.

.. versionadded:: 0.14.0

The result reproduces :meth:`solve` as a pure function of a parameter
pytree (pulse parameters, interaction strengths, detunings, decay scale,
or sampled input fields), so the propagated field and any loss of it can
be differentiated exactly with JAX autodiff. Requires the ``jax`` extra
(``pip install 'clerq[jax]'``) and ``jax_enable_x64``.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name      | Type   | Description                                                                                                                | Default   |
|-----------|--------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------|
| **options | Any    | forwarded to :class:`clerq.autodiff.AutodiffPropagation` (``step``, ``strategy``, ``rtol``, ``atol``, ``max_steps``, ...). | `{}`      |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type   | Description                                             |
|--------|--------|---------------------------------------------------------|
|        | Any    | The differentiable problem, an ``AutodiffPropagation``. |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                | Description                                                                              |
|--------|---------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | ImportError         | if the ``jax`` extra is not installed.                                                   |
|        | NotImplementedError | for counter-propagating fields or pulse functions the autodiff backend does not support. |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> ad = solver.to_autodiff()
>>> value, grads = ad.value_and_grad(loss)
```
